patch.value: Semicolon-free exported variables consume following declarations

parseExportedVar has no automatic-semicolon-insertion boundary for an exported variable statement. A semicolon-free export followed on a new line by another declaration is consumed as initializer syntax, so the following binding is never judged.
Semicolon-free export followed by another export judges both bindings; Multiline conditional, call, type, and grouped initializers are not split prematurely
Analyze a documented export const first = 1 without a semicolon followed by an undocumented export const second = 2; observe only first is counted and no second violation is reported.
ASI terminates the first variable statement at a declaration boundary and the following export is independently judged.
The parser consumes tokens through the following declaration until a semicolon, closing brace, or EOF.
Undocumented exports can bypass a gate advertised as fail-closed.

value.author: harness:codex
value.text: Variable-statement recovery needs an explicit post-loop return because the tokenizer omits an EOF token; otherwise a semicolon-free final declarator re-enters the outer declarator loop and creates a synthetic fail-closed violation.

patch.value: Focused regression passes 2/2 together with the symlink-cycle test; two semicolon-free exports are counted independently, the undocumented second binding is reported, and a grouped multiline initializer remains intact.

Added declaration-start and expression-end token sets, stopped semicolon-free variable recovery only at a valid newline declaration boundary, and returned cleanly after an EOF-terminated final declarator.
ASI-aware declaration boundaries and EOF recovery now preserve following exports and multiline initializers.
